prompt:
Need to send my weekly status to Director Chen about the data platform migration. Raw notes:

- moved the customer_orders table family (14 tables, ~2.3M rows) to the new cluster on Tuesday, validation scripts pass, no integrity issues
- inventory tables BLOCKED - waiting on answer about whether we keep the legacy status_code column or map to the new enum values, came up in schema review
- freeze date currently March 15 but we need a go/no-go from Chen by end of week
- migration about 35% complete by table count
- downstream consumers notified about the customer_orders move, no complaints so far

Draft the status update for me. Chen needs to decide whether we stick with the March 15 freeze date or push it, and whether to keep or drop that legacy column.

Need to update VP Martinez on the PayStream to NovaPay switch. Notes:

- ran 847 test transactions last week, all passed, avg latency 230ms vs 310ms on old provider
- USD EUR GBP all green
- JPY still untested - NovaPay sandbox has a bug on their end, they said fix coming by Friday but who knows
- cutover date April 3 is looking tight if we can't test JPY this week
- we process roughly 12K JPY transactions per month, can't skip it
- rollback plan tested and ready, takes about 45 minutes
- compliance signed off on everything except JPY obviously
- not sure if NovaPay will actually deliver that sandbox fix on time

Write this up for Martinez. She needs to decide whether to keep the April 3 cutover or delay until JPY testing completes.

Putting together my update for Sarah Kim the program sponsor on the network refresh across our three sites:

- Site A (Detroit) done Feb 12, 340 endpoints migrated, zero escalations
- Site B (Austin) done Feb 28, 215 endpoints, 2 minor switch config issues fixed same day
- Site C (Portland) DELAYED - the 48-port switches got pushed back, now arriving March 18 instead of March 4, vendor says port congestion in Seattle
- original budget was $1.2M, currently at $1.23M with the Portland delay (storage costs, extended contractor hours)
- Portland has 280 endpoints, biggest site
- not sure if we can absorb the overage or need to request additional funds
- contractor rates go up April 1 if we extend

Draft the status for Kim. She needs to decide whether to approve the budget overage or if we should cut scope somewhere to compensate.

Weekly update for Rachel Torres head of CS on onboarding times:

- median onboarding time dropped from 14.2 days to 11.8 days this quarter
- enterprise segment improved from 22 days to 18 days
- mid-market went from 9 days to 7.5 days
- BUT small business segment went from 6 days to 8.3 days - they're hitting more setup issues with the new config flow we rolled out in January
- we think we need another onboarding specialist for the small biz team, currently have 3 handling ~90 new accounts/month
- also not sure if we should simplify the small biz flow or just add headcount
- NPS scores holding steady at 41 overall
- small biz NPS dropped from 38 to 31 though

Write this up for Torres. She needs to decide whether to hire another onboarding specialist or push for a flow redesign first.

Need my daily update for the project tracker on the API gateway rollout:

- successfully moved the billing service to the new gateway yesterday, 4 hours of traffic with no errors, p99 latency 89ms
- attempted to move the notifications service, had to rollback after 25 minutes - connection pool exhaustion, error rates spiked to 12%
- rollback completed cleanly, notifications back on old gateway
- root cause appears to be the notifications service opens more persistent connections than we modeled, probably 3x more
- not sure when our next migration window is - need to coordinate with the notifications team and they're on a release freeze until March 22
- 6 services remaining after billing
- 2 of those 6 also have high connection counts

Write this up for the tracker. The steering committee needs to decide whether to proceed with other services while we wait for the notifications team or pause the whole rollout.

Need to send a note to Finance Director Park about our CloudBase credits:

- we have $87,400 in credits remaining as of March 1
- current burn rate is approximately $14,200/month
- credits expire June 30 if not used or renewed
- option 1: accelerate some planned Q3 workloads into Q2 to use credits before expiry, probably 2-3 projects
- option 2: negotiate a credit extension or renewal with CloudBase
- I don't know what renewal terms CloudBase would offer - our account rep left last month and new one hasn't been assigned yet, I've asked for an intro
- if we do nothing we'll have about $44,800 in unused credits at expiry
- our contract minimum spend is $10K/month regardless

Write this up for Park. She needs to decide whether to push for a renewal negotiation or restructure our workload timeline to burn down the credits.

Putting together beta program update for Product Director Williams:

- 312 sign-ups as of March 5, up from 287 last week
- 89 users completed full onboarding flow
- 47 users dropped off after step 2 (the permissions grant step)
- 23 users dropped off after step 4 (first data import)
- one escalation from Meridian Corp - their admin says the SSO integration is broken, getting 403 errors intermittently, our team is investigating, got 3 support tickets from them
- average session time for active users is 18.4 minutes
- 14 users have submitted feedback through the in-app form
- beta is scheduled to run through April 15
- not sure if Meridian is a one-off or if other SSO users are hitting the same thing, still digging

Draft the update for Williams. This is informational only, no decisions needed from her right now.

Writing handoff notes for Priya who takes over on-call tomorrow about the email delivery issue:

- intermittent email delivery delays started Monday, affecting roughly 8-12% of outbound messages
- delays range from 3 minutes to 45 minutes
- ruled out: DNS issues (checked), SMTP server health (all green), queue backlog (normal), our code changes (last deploy was 2 weeks before issues started)
- ruled out: downstream provider issues (their status page clean, direct tests pass)
- current theory: something in the TLS handshake with certain receiving servers, seeing occasional renegotiation loops in logs
- enabled additional logging on the mail relay at 2pm today
- don't know when we'll have enough data from the new logs to confirm the theory - could be hours or could take a couple days given the intermittent nature
- no customer-facing SLA breaches yet but we're getting close on 3 accounts

Write this up for Priya. She'll need to monitor the new logs and decide if/when to escalate to the mail relay vendor.

Need to send status to CTO Anand on the security patch campaign:

- Tier 1 (critical): 23 of 24 systems patched, the remaining one is the old auth service running on Solaris - vendor doesn't have a patch for CVE-2024-4487
- Tier 2 (high): 41 of 48 systems patched, 7 in progress, expect done by March 20
- Tier 3 (medium): 12 of 35 systems patched, slower going because of change windows
- the Solaris auth service can't be patched and can't be upgraded without a full rewrite (estimated 3-4 months)
- it's behind our firewall but still technically in scope for the compliance audit April 15
- we need to file an exception request with the security team, not sure if they'll accept compensating controls or require us to take it offline
- it handles about 2,100 internal auth requests per day
- could potentially isolate it further with network segmentation as a compensating control

Write this up for Anand. He needs to decide whether to approve the exception request and what compensating controls to propose, or commit to taking the service offline.

Sprint 47 summary for Design Lead Marcus:

Shipped:
- DASH-882 new filter bar on the inventory page, 3 components
- DASH-901 updated empty state illustrations, 5 screens
- DASH-915 search results layout refactor

Slipped:
